we have created an automated system that can model a person's attitudes, beliefs, and opinions, and that this system can be used in an application that provides the just-in-time opinions of people whose opinions matter to a user.

(i) the opinions of people who are important to us are a powerful source of feedback for our own work, and (ii) we can automatically model a person's opinions, and then use this model to provide just-in-time feedback to the user.

In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of systems that are able to understand people, and that help people understand each other.
how people can better understand each other, and how computers can help.
the design of a system which will enable a computer to understand a person's personality, attitudes, and opinions, and to provide feedback to that person based on those understandings.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this paper presents a novel method for modeling the attitudes and opinions of a person and a proactive interface which uses this model to provide the user with a just-in-time perspective of people whose opinions he cares about.
we are able to model a person's attitude and opinions and use that to provide feedback to a user.
the What Would They Think? system is able to model a person's attitudes in a way that is more effective than other methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our system is a step toward a new class of intelligent user interfaces which can help people learn about others' perspectives in a way that would be impossible without technology.
we have developed a novel method for automated attitude modeling, a proactive interface for presenting the modeled attitudes, and a set of empirical studies that validate the approach.
it is possible to build a model of the attitudes and opinions of people, and that such models are valuable for helping people to learn more effectively.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the right people are often not available to provide the right feedback at the right time, and that computational models of people can provide a useful alternative.
a computational model of a person's attitudes can be used to help us understand that person's opinions and perspectives.
